items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07
items.q: I had Albert Jive on drums, D on trumpet, I'm on piano, just three pieces.

ctx.x: Who was with you at this place at St. Bernard and St. Claude?
Let me see. Who had one drum? Was it Albert Jive? Albert. Right. I had Albert Jive on drums, D on trumpet, I'm on piano, just three pieces.
And from there you went to Bunky?

items.title: De De Pierce Interview, 1960-01-10
items.q: I said, well, Billy, I left Billy home sick and Billy wouldn't follow no parade.

ctx.x: And he told me, look on the back, look who Billy liked that. I said, I know that ain't Billy on the back. And my goodness, I'll tell you the truth, if that wasn't Billy in a way, I'll eat my hat. It ain't no joke. Who could be Billy's twin? I got out the line and run the door and grab her, you know. And the woman faced me and I saw it with me and I suppose she had a boy in front of something in the line like this fella there believing in the dice, I would have got hurt. Yeah. You know, and I come back there and…
I saw John today on the bus. He got on the bus.

items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02
items.q: And then from then I hired Willie to go with me, to work with me, being my wife, you see.

ctx.x: And that's why he was little down and looking to work him.
Yeah, if I take the job over, so. And then from then I hired Willie to go with me, to work with me, being my wife, you see. Yeah.

Well, there's one thing I forgot to ask Billy about your singing. Who were some of the best blues singers or other, any kind of singers that you heard when you were younger, coming up? That you, in other words, did you listen to any singers that you liked and maybe learnt from them? Something you could take lessons? Yeah, one for one. Who's that?

items.title: Billie Pierce, De De Pierce, Israel Gorman, Joseph "Kid Twat" Butler Interview, 1963-11-20
items.q: What year did y'all get married in? About 1935. By 1934.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. We just lived together. Bill Rossman. Yeah, we're watching.

Yeah, actually, for all the nice boys and David Wyckoff, they were the ones who put up the money for the kids, I remember now. Let's see. Maybe I can get you to turn it off for a minute now, okay? Off. Time to start off. I don't know. Oh, no, I haven't been to Florida. Have you been to Florida? Where are you from? I'm from Florida. What part? Pensacola. Pensacola? Yeah. Can I embarrass you? What's your age? Now, what year were you born in? 1970. Born in 1970 over there? And what's your exact birthday? June the…

See? What are they calling you now? It's from the Boudoir. It has to be from the Boudoir. That's my handle. That's the handle you put on that. Well, the Boudoir, you see, I'm going to show you a lot of people don't know what a Boudoir is. You see, when I came down here from Memphis, you see, and I was cigarette test up there, and you go in there and smoke and test them cigarettes. That's what you call a Boudoir. What kind of cigarettes?
